previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old male with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, coronary artery disease, and type 2 diabetes presented with acute substernal chest pain, bradycardia, and nausea after a shower. He was found to have severe hyperkalemia (K+ 6.7) with ECG changes including peaked T waves and first-degree AV block. He received emergency treatment with calcium gluconate, insulin, dextrose, sodium bicarbonate, and Kayexalate, followed by emergent hemodialysis. His potassium normalized, chest pain resolved, and ECG returned to baseline. Serial troponins were stable, indicating no acute myocardial infarction. He remained hemodynamically stable on telemetry, completed a scheduled dialysis session, and was discharged home in good condition with medication adjustments and dietary instructions to avoid high-potassium foods.

hyperkalemia. Troponins x3 unremarkable. Patient ambulated prior 
to discharge and remained chest pain free.

hypoaldosteronism, type 1 RTA, or fasting in the setting of CKD.

potassium diet. Nephrology was consulted. They will continue to 
assess him in dialysis, and will consider outpatient kayexelate 
on non dialysis days.
